chunks: Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from al-Barqi, from Abi Hashim al-Ja'fari who said: I heard Ali b. Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him) saying:

My God, Your power is manifest but Your form is not. Because of this they became ignorant of You and with that (ignorance) estimated You. While the (true) estimation is other than how they described You. And I am disassociated, O My God, from those who sought You by likening You (to Your creatures). There is nothing like You. My God, they will never reach You. What is apparent of Your blessings around them is an indicator towards You. If only they recognized You. And in Your creation, O My God, there is ample to understand You. However, they equated You to Your creation and because of that did not attain recognition of You. They took some of Your signs as Lord (instead of You) and with that (imperfect attributes) described You. Elevated are You, My Lord, from that which the Likeners impute to You.

key_terms.الْمُشَبِّهُونَ: The Likeners (those who attribute likeness to God)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia theological perspective on God's form and likeness according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This supplication from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) articulates the Shia doctrine of *tanzih* (divine transcendence) by distinguishing between God's manifest power (*qudrah*) and His unseen essence (*hay'ah*), critiquing anthropomorphists who project created forms onto the Divine. It emphasizes that while creation points to the Creator, superficial observers mistakenly equate God with His signs, leading to *tashbih* (likeness). The text serves as a theological defense against those who limit the Infinite by using finite human attributes, affirming that God is beyond all description and comparison.
